\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textbf{Aggregation level} (4 of 61 shown)}\\[1pt]
\texttt{chinook\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{1adc54e3cf} & Which media types (by name, counting only tracks that have a media type) have a bytes-per-millisecond rate higher than the simple average of that rate across all media types? For each, show the media type name, its rate, and how much it exceeds that average, unrounded. & \textbf{A:} Each media type's rate is the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios; list the media types whose rate is above the unweighted mean of all media types' rates, with the rate and how far above it is.\newline \textbf{B:} Each media type's rate is its total Bytes divided by its total Milliseconds; list the media types whose rate is above the unweighted mean of all media types' rates, with the rate and how far above it is. & value 181.7 vs 179.5 & \texttt{-\,B\,B\,N}\\[2pt]
\texttt{formula\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{c759056a31} & For each circuit country, what are the average constructor standings points and wins (the season-to-date figures) at races held there? Also, how far is each country's average wins above or below the average of the country figures? & \textbf{A:} A country's averages are the mean of per-race averages, so each race counts equally.\newline \textbf{B:} A country's averages are the plain mean over all of its standings records pooled together. & value 0.039 vs -0.03776 & \texttt{S\,-\,-\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{thrombosis\_\allowbreak{}prediction}\newline \texttt{7fd142e2d9} & By patient sex, what are the average aCL IgG and ANA values in the examination data (only examinations linked to a patient, missing values ignored)? Also give each sex's average ANA as a ratio of the mean of the per-sex ANA averages, unrounded. & \textbf{A:} Average aCL IgG and ANA over all matched examination records within each sex. Each examination counts once.\newline \textbf{B:} Average each patient's examinations into per-patient values first. Then average those values within each sex, so each patient counts once. & value 3.281 vs 3.334 & \texttt{S\,S\,S\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{alien}\newline \texttt{cde68b2348} & For observatory stations whose average telescope bandwidth usage (\texttt{bandusagepct}) is above average, what is their mean bandwidth usage, and how far above average are they on average? Ignore missing usage values, and give both figures unrounded in a single row. & \textbf{A:} Compare each station's average bandwidth usage with the unweighted mean of the station averages.\newline \textbf{B:} Compare each station's average bandwidth usage with the mean bandwidth usage over all individual telescopes. & value 24.9 vs 25.03 & \texttt{S\,B\,B\,N}\\[2pt]
\midrule
\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textbf{Counting unit} (4 of 47 shown)}\\[1pt]
\texttt{sakila\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{fc16192583} & For each actor, show their actor ID, how many films they're credited in, that count as a fraction of the total, and how far that fraction is above or below the average fraction across actors. Return the top 10 by that difference, highest first, unrounded. & \textbf{A:} Each actor's film count is divided by the total number of casting credits in film\_actor, which gives the actor's share of all credits.\newline \textbf{B:} Each actor's film count is divided by the number of distinct films that have a cast in film\_actor, which gives the fraction of those films the actor appears in. & value 0.001591 vs 0.008716 & \texttt{-\,N\,-\,-}\\[2pt]
\texttt{formula\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{c1a8ce4d18} & Which circuit cities have an above-average share of qualifying? For each, show the city, its qualifying count, that count as a share of the total across all cities, and how far its share is above the average city share (all unrounded). & \textbf{A:} Each city's count is its number of driver qualifying entries, and its share is its share of all qualifying entries.\newline \textbf{B:} Each city's count is its number of distinct races with qualifying data (qualifying sessions), and its share is its share of all such sessions. & 16 vs 17 rows & \texttt{S\,S\,-\,-}\\[2pt]
\texttt{student\_\allowbreak{}club}\newline \texttt{6b346d7be2} & Taking attendance entries that match an event (others left out), how many attendees does each event \texttt{status} have, and what share of the total across all statuses is that? Show the status, its number of attendees, and the share, without rounding. & \textbf{A:} A status's attendance is the total number of member-event attendance entries for events with that status.\newline \textbf{B:} A status's attendance is the number of different members who attended any event with that status. & value 297 vs 30 & \texttt{S\,B\,S\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{insider}\newline \texttt{e6f24d2438} & For each trader type, how many analysed trade records are there in the advanced behaviour data (only where the trade and its trader can be found), and what share of the overall total does each type make up? Keep the share unrounded. & \textbf{A:} For each trader type, count the advanced behaviour analysis records that join to a transaction and a trader. Report that count and its share of the total count over all trader types.\newline \textbf{B:} For each trader type, count the distinct transactions that have at least one advanced behaviour analysis and a matching trader. Report that count and its share of the total count over all trader types. & value 242 vs 241 & \texttt{B\,B\,B\,S}\\[2pt]
\midrule
\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textbf{Missing values} (4 of 29 shown)}\\[1pt]
\texttt{baseball\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{f74c2bad9d} & For players who received award votes (matched to \texttt{player} by \texttt{player\_\allowbreak{}id}), what is the average \texttt{points\_\allowbreak{}won} for each death country (ignoring missing points)? Show each death country, its average, and how far it is from the simple average of those per-country averages, without rounding. & \textbf{A:} Average the points won per death country, with a blank death country kept as its own group. Compare each group's average with the plain average of all group averages, the blank group included.\newline \textbf{B:} Average the points won per death country, leaving out players with no recorded death country. Compare each country's average with the plain average of the remaining countries' averages. & 8 vs 7 rows & \texttt{N\,N\,-\,N}\\[2pt]
\texttt{formula\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{af91f25689} & Which 10 drivers have the most qualifying entries compared with the average driver? For each, show the driver ID, how many qualifying records they have, and that number divided by the average number of qualifying records per driver (unrounded), highest ratio first. & \textbf{A:} The average number of qualifying records per driver is computed only over drivers who appear in the qualifying table.\newline \textbf{B:} The average number of qualifying records per driver is computed over every driver in the drivers table, with drivers who never qualified counting as zero. & value 4.112 vs 22.63 & \texttt{S\,B\,B\,B}\\[2pt]
\texttt{student\_\allowbreak{}club}\newline \texttt{55be105b98} & Group members by their major (\texttt{link\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}major}) and show each major id, how many members it has, and that count's share of the total. List the top 10 by share, highest first, with no rounding. & \textbf{A:} Members without a major form their own group, and they are included in the total used as the denominator.\newline \textbf{B:} Members without a major are left out of both the groups and the total used as the denominator. & 10 rows; 1 differ & \texttt{B\,B\,B\,N}\\[2pt]
\texttt{crypto}\newline \texttt{b61f4a52bd} & For each order in \texttt{orderexecutions.\allowbreak{}ordersmark} (executions with no order reference grouped together), what's the average size (\texttt{fillcount}) of the fills it got? Keep the orders whose average beats the average across all orders, and note by how much. Then, among those, keep the ones that also beat that group's own average, and note that margin too. Give me one summary row with three values: the average per-order fill size of the final orders, their average margin over the first benchmark, and their average margin over the second. Leave everything unrounded. & \textbf{A:} Zero-quantity executions count as fills of 0 in each order's average fill quantity.\newline \textbf{B:} Zero-quantity executions are not fills and are left out of each order's average fill quantity. & value 4.024 vs 4.021 & \texttt{S\,S\,S\,S}\\[2pt]
\midrule
\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textbf{Negation} (1 of 1 shown)}\\[1pt]
\texttt{customers\_\allowbreak{}and\_\allowbreak{}invoices}\newline \texttt{2e529bb193}\newline (filter) & Ignoring transactions with no invoice number, which invoice numbers have transactions without the type 'Payment' (exact text)? Show each invoice number with the total number of transactions recorded for it. Sort by that count from highest to lowest and give the top 10. & \textbf{A:} Invoices with no Payment transaction at all. For each one, count its transactions and show the top 10 by count.\newline \textbf{B:} Invoices with at least one transaction that is not a Payment. \multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textbf{Strict cutoff} (4 of 42 shown)}\\[1pt]
\texttt{chinook\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{06934ae88f}\newline (filter) & Using 3.98 as the cutoff on the invoice total (\texttt{Invoice.\allowbreak{}Total}) to keep only the higher-value invoices, what is their average total, as a single unrounded value? Ignore missing totals, and give a missing result if no invoices qualify. & \textbf{A:} Invoices whose total equals 3.98 are included in the average.\newline \textbf{B:} Only invoices whose total is strictly greater than 3.98 are included in the average. & 1 rows; 1 differ & \texttt{B\,B\,B\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{financial}\newline \texttt{8a55588ad2}\newline (filter) & Applying a cutoff of 2802.0 to the debited amount (\texttt{order.\allowbreak{}amount}), what is the average debited amount of the large standing orders, unrounded? & \textbf{A:} Orders of exactly 2802.0 are included.\newline \textbf{B:} Only orders above 2802.0 are included. & 1 rows; 1 differ & \texttt{B\,B\,B\,B}\\[2pt]
\texttt{formula\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{57277c47b4}\newline (filter) & Among driver standings entries where the driver has upwards of 1 point so far that season, what is the average season-to-date win count? Ignore missing values and don't round. & \textbf{A:} Average the season-to-date win counts over standings entries whose season-to-date points are 1 or more.\newline \textbf{B:} Average the season-to-date win counts over standings entries whose season-to-date points are more than 1. & 1 rows; 1 differ & \texttt{B\,B\,B\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{insider}\newline \texttt{8ed79619ea}\newline (filter) & Using 0.149 as the cutoff, how many advanced behaviour records have high peer correlation (\texttt{peercorr})? Give a single count. & \textbf{A:} Peer correlation values equal to 0.149 are counted (at least 0.149).\newline \textbf{B:} Only peer correlation values strictly greater than 0.149 are counted (more than 0.149). & 1 rows; 1 differ & \texttt{B\,B\,B\,N}\\[2pt]
\midrule
\multicolumn{5}{@{}l}{\textbf{Ties and selection} (4 of 24 shown)}\\[1pt]
\texttt{sakila\_\allowbreak{}1}\newline \texttt{b77a784ee8} & What are the top 10 films by number of copies in our inventory? For each, show the \texttt{film\_\allowbreak{}id}, how many copies we have, and what share of all inventory copies that is (copies divided by the total number of copies, unrounded), with the highest share first. & \textbf{A:} List the top 10 films by share of inventory copies, returning exactly 10 rows and choosing arbitrarily among films tied at the cut.\newline \textbf{B:} List the top films by share of inventory copies, keeping every film whose copy count reaches the 10th-highest count, so ties at the cut are all included. & 10 vs 72 rows & \texttt{-\,N\,-\,-}\\[2pt]
\texttt{financial}\newline \texttt{53afca1d49} & What are the top 10 branch districts (\texttt{account.\allowbreak{}district\_\allowbreak{}id}) by share of all accounts? For each, show the district id, its number of accounts and its share of all accounts, without rounding, listed from the highest share down. & \textbf{A:} Rank districts by their share of accounts and return exactly the first 10 rows, dropping tied districts arbitrarily at the cut.\newline \textbf{B:} Rank districts by their share of accounts and return every district whose share reaches the 10th-highest share, including all ties at the cut. & 10 vs 12 rows & \texttt{S\,N\,S\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{student\_\allowbreak{}club}\newline \texttt{5c048dd871} & Which are the top 10 members by share of total event attendance? Match attendance to members by member id, count attendance per member id and position, and show the member id, position, attendance count and share of all attendance, from highest share to lowest. & \textbf{A:} Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return exactly 10 rows, cutting arbitrarily through any tie at 10th place.\newline \textbf{B:} Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return the top 10 plus every row tied with the 10th row's share. & 10 vs 12 rows & \texttt{S\,N\,S\,S}\\[2pt]
\texttt{alien}\newline \texttt{ee6b268047} & What are the top 10 telescopes by share of detected signals? For each telescope reference (\texttt{telescref}), show how many signals it detected and what fraction of all signals that is (unrounded), from the largest share down. & \textbf{A:} Rank telescopes by their share of all signals and return exactly 10 rows, choosing arbitrarily among telescopes tied at the 10th place.\newline \textbf{B:} Rank telescopes by their share of all signals and return every telescope whose share is at least the 10th-highest share, including all ties at the cut. & 10 vs 51 rows & \texttt{-\,N\,S\,-}\\[2pt]
